what_this_measures: ESDI measures DISRUPTION EXPOSURE, not measured capacity loss.
For each sector it answers: what share of the installed base sits at facilities
disrupted recently enough to still be plausibly impaired, weighted by how strong
the evidence is and how long ago it happened.
It is NOT a claim about actual lost throughput or generation. Open reporting
almost never states how much capacity a given strike removed, and this project
does not invent that number. Where a source does quantify the loss, the figure is
carried on the incident and shown, but the index itself is exposure-based so that
quantified and unquantified incidents are treated on the same defensible footing.

confidence_weights._comment: Evidence strength for whether the event occurred. Applied multiplicatively.

cause_weights._comment: How much a cause implies unplanned impairment. Scheduled maintenance is planned downtime and is near-discounted; sanctions bite gradually rather than removing capacity outright.

_comment: Recovery / reconstitution model (iteration 1). Replaces the flat repair half-life.
Impairment decays as 0.5^(days_since_disruption / effective_half_life). The
effective half-life is EVIDENCE-DRIVEN, in priority order:
1. observed reconstitution/restoration duration from a source  (kind=observed)
2. an estimated reconstitution window from a source             (kind=estimated)
3. the modelled sector fallback below                          (kind=modelled)
A reconstitution horizon H (disruption -> substantially restored) maps to a half-life
of H / horizon_to_halflife_factor, so impairment is ~reconstitution_residual at H.
Observed recovery evidence therefore overrides the generic assumption, which is the
whole point: a sourced restart matters more than a half-life guess. See recovery.py.

sector_fallback_horizon_days._comment: MODELLED full-reconstitution horizons in days, used ONLY when an incident carries no observed or estimated recovery evidence. Assumptions, flagged kind=modelled in output. Chosen so the implied half-life matches the previous model (H = old_half_life x 3.32), keeping the index continuous while re-framing it as a reconstitution horizon. Still the weakest input; replace with evidence.

recovery._partial_note: When a source reports partial operations resumed but not full reconstitution, impairment is held no lower than this until full reconstitution evidence arrives -- a restart is not a return to full capability.

_comment: Iteration 2: recovery is now INCIDENT-level and evidence precedence is RULE-based,
not confidence-as-a-multiplier. A recovery record only overrides the model if its
source confidence clears min_confidence_to_override.
fully_reconstituted (conf>=min): closes the incident -> impairment capped at the
residual from the reconstitution date. Terminology: substantially restored to
full capability, per a credible source.
substantially_restored (conf>=min): observed days become the reconstitution horizon.
a sourced ESTIMATE (conf>=min): its central value becomes the horizon (kind=estimated).
partial_restart: DISPLAY ONLY. Records the observed restart date but does NOT
accelerate decay and NEVER implies full restoration -- 'operations resumed' is not
'fully reconstituted'. Scoring falls back to the modelled horizon.
low-confidence estimate (conf<min): shown in the UI but does NOT drive the decay curve.
otherwise: modelled sector fallback.
Priority: observed full/substantial > credible sourced estimate > modelled fallback.

status_multipliers._comment: Applied when a source explicitly states the recovery state, overriding pure time decay. 'repaired' collapses the contribution; 'active' holds it at full decayed value.

sector_weights._comment: Contribution of each sector to the national composite. A judgement call about systemic importance, not a measured quantity. Sums to 1.0.

sector_basis._comment: What denominator each sector's exposure is measured against. 'capacity' uses MW or MTPA; 'count' falls back to number of assets because the class has no published capacity figure. Count-based sectors are flagged in the output so the UI can mark them as weaker measures.

cutoff._comment: An incident stops contributing once decayed below this, to keep the time series from carrying a long meaningless tail.

timeline._comment: Weekly steps. Daily resolution would quadruple the payload without changing any visible conclusion, since the decay half-lives are measured in weeks.
